name: Galerie im Alten Rathaus
kurzbeschreibung: Museum Kitzbühel / Sammlung Alfons Walde at Hinterstadt 32 features 60 original Walde paintings, mining history, and a panoramic rooftop terrace.
oeffnungszeiten: Sommer täglich 10:00–17:00 Uhr (Do bis 20:00 Uhr), Winter Di–So 14:00–18:00 Uhr (Sa ab 10:00)
beschreibung:
Overview

The tradition-rich Museum Kitzbühel – Sammlung Alfons Walde (historically also recorded in municipal records in the context of the Galerie im Alten Rathaus) is located at Hinterstadt 32 in the heritage-protected historic center of the chamois town of Kitzbühel. Housed within the venerable walls of the former municipal granary and a medieval southwest tower of the town fortifications, the venue forms Kitzbühel's illustrious cultural centerpiece. Across several modernized exhibition floors, the museum unites world-famous masterpieces of Tyrolean modernism with the fascinating history of regional mining and Kitzbühel skiing.

Sammlung Alfons Walde & Town History

The historic building dates back to the first half of the 16th century and was adapted as a municipal granary at the beginning of the 18th century. Founded in the 1930s as a local heritage museum, the building was sensitively expanded architecturally over the decades. The absolute highlight of the museum is the world's largest permanent exhibition dedicated to the work of the renowned Kitzbühel painter and architect Alfons Walde (1891–1958). In the light-flooded top-floor galleries, visitors can admire over 60 original oil paintings as well as around 100 drawings, pastels, and poster designs. Walde's iconic snowscapes, sun-drenched farmhouses, and dynamic paintings of skiers shaped the Alpine lifestyle and made Kitzbühel internationally famous as a winter sports metropolis. In addition to the art collection, the museum illuminates the region's more than 3,000-year-old mining tradition—from Bronze Age copper extraction to modern silver mining—as well as the glorious era of the Kitzbühel ski wonder team centered around exceptional athlete Toni Sailer.

Visit & Getting There

Museum Kitzbühel is accessible year-round with seasonal opening hours: in the summer season (July to September) daily from 10:00 to 17:00 (Thursdays long museum evening until 20:00); in the winter season (late November to April) Tuesday to Sunday from 14:00 to 18:00 and Saturday from 10:00 to 18:00; during the shoulder seasons Tuesday to Friday from 10:00 to 13:00 and Saturday from 10:00 to 17:00. Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €9.00, groups of 10 or more €7.00, children and youth up to 18 years enjoy free admission. Arrival by train: via ÖBB to Kitzbühel station or Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm stop, followed by an easy five-minute walk through the traffic-calmed pedestrian zone to Hinterstadt 32. By car: via B161 (Pass-Thurn-Straße) to Kitzbühel, parking is available at Pfarrau or at the Hahnenkamm parking lot.

Tips

Following a comprehensive redesign, the entire museum is fully wheelchair-accessible and barrier-free thanks to a modern passenger elevator and step-free transitions. An absolute highlight in summer is a visit to the museum rooftop terrace on the former defensive tower: from there, a spectacular 360-degree panoramic view opens up over the colorful gabled facades of the Kitzbühel old town, the Hahnenkamm with the world-famous Streif, and the Kitzbüheler Horn.
